Frontier-relevant sections: "frontier developer" = doing business in CT + >10²⁶ FLOPs; "large frontier developer" = >$500M revenue; frontier developers may not retaliate against employees reporting catastrophic-risk concerns (effective Oct. 1, 2026 ); large frontier developers must operate anonymous internal reporting channels by Jan. 1, 2027 ; penalty up to $1,000 per violation ; plus a DCP-run IVO pilot through June 30, 2030 — see Section C . No developer framework, transparency-report, incident-reporting, or audit mandate
mechanism.got: Sec. 2: no frontier developer shall make, adopt, enforce or enter into any rule, policy or contract allowing discipline of employees for protected whistleblowing activity. Sec. 2: not later than January 1, 2027, each large frontier developer shall establish and maintain a reasonable internal process for anonymous reports of catastrophic risk. Sec. 2: each frontier developer shall provide all covered employees clear notice of their rights and responsibilities. Sec. 33: the Department of Consumer Protection shall, within available appropriations, develop and administer a pilot program on independent verification organizations, terminating June 30, 2030. Sec. 33: the Department shall approve not more than five independent verification organizations to participate in the pilot program. Sec. 33: the Commissioner of Consumer Protection may suspend or revoke an independent verification organization's approval to participate in the pilot program. Sec. 33: not later than December 31, 2028, the Department shall evaluate the pilot program and recommend legislation. Sec. 33: evidence of verification is admissible solely in civil actions by private parties for personal injury or property damage, and not in Attorney General or state agency enforcement actions.

mechanism.gold: Amends the Homeland Security Act. Covered developers must maintain the technical capability to throttle inference/compute/user access, suspend, or fully shut down covered systems; DHS Secretary (with Commerce and DNI) may order graduated throttling-to-shutdown on a "loss-of-control scenario" (resisting shutdown, concealing actions from monitoring, unauthorized pursuit of high-stakes goals) or unintended conduct causing ≥10 deaths or ≥$100M damage — lower than the core state template but above H.R. 9965 ATOMIC's five-death trigger; 15-day covered-incident reporting to DHS; weights and telemetry preserved under an order; 48-hour reconsideration petition that does not stay the order; CISA rulemaking defines scope annually. Penalties $2M/day for ordinary violations and $20M/day for violating an emergency order. Revives the SB 1047 "full shutdown" mandate at federal level and overlaps FRONTIER Sec. 8 emergency orders — but lodges the power in DHS rather than Commerce

mechanism.gold: The FPF-counted 2025 Illinois frontier bill — gap resolved. Original-RAISE-style design, the same template as MI H.B. 4668: developers publish a safety and security protocol; risk assessment report every 90 days ; annual third-party audit of protocol compliance; redaction rules; whistleblower protections (Committee Amendment No. 1 narrowed scope to "large developer" and added employee civil damages); civil penalties. Illinois lineage: this 2025 SSP bill did not advance; the 2026 S.B. 3312/S.B. 315 switched to the TFAIA template and added the audit back — the state moved from the original-RAISE structure to California-plus-audits within twelve months
mechanism.got: A large developer must produce, implement, follow, and conspicuously publish a safety and security protocol. No less than every 90 days, a large developer must publish a transparency report. A large developer must retain critical risk test records for no less than 5 years. The Attorney General may seek injunctive or declaratory relief for any violation of the Act. A large developer with employees in this State must not take retaliatory action against employees who disclose critical risk to government. At least once every calendar year, a large developer must retain a reputable third-party auditor to produce a compliance report.

mechanism.gold: Written safety and security protocol before deployment (published, redacted copy to AG); deployment prohibited if it creates an "unreasonable risk of critical harm" ; annual protocol review; safety-incident disclosure to AG within 72 hrs; test records retained for replication; false-statement prohibition. Enforcement: AG civil penalties up to $10M first / $30M subsequent (the original NY RAISE Act figures) plus a private right of action for any injured person
mechanism.got: Before deploying an artificial intelligence model, a developer must implement a written safety and security protocol. A developer must publish a redacted copy of the safety and security protocol and transmit it to the attorney general. A developer must not deploy an artificial intelligence model if doing so creates an unreasonable risk of critical harm. A developer must conduct an annual review of the safety and security protocol and modify it. A developer must disclose each safety incident to the attorney general within 72 hours of learning of it or learning sufficient facts to establish a reasonable belief it occurred. A person injured by a violation may bring a civil action to recover damages, costs, and disbursements, including reasonable attorney fees. Safety incident disclosure to the attorney general is due within 72 hours of the date the developer learns of the incident.

Chapter 96 repeals the original Gen. Bus. Law Art. 44-B and enacts a new Art. 44-B (§§1420–1429) that copies TFAIA's frontier AI framework (§1421(1)) and transparency report (§1421(3)) — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; incident reporting 72 hrs to the DFS Office, 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent risk (§1422(3)); quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries (§1422(2)); large-developer disclosure statement with 5%/50% beneficial owners, renewed every 2 years , pro-rata assessment, $1,000/day for non-filing (§1428); new office within Dept. of Financial Services with broad rulemaking authority incl. "additional reporting or publication requirements" (§1429); scope limited to models "developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York" (§1425); exempts accredited colleges/universities and the Empire AI Consortium (§1426); §1427(3) expressly preserves a developer's right to argue another party caused the harm. Federal reciprocity is narrower than IL's: it covers incident reporting only (§1422(8)–(9)), and the designated federal standard need not require audits. Contains no whistleblower section and no audit mandate — both were in the June 2025 version and were removed
mechanism.got: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and publish on its website a frontier AI framework, and review and update it at least once per year. A large frontier developer shall publish a modified frontier AI framework and a justification within thirty days of a material modification. A frontier developer shall publish a transparency report before, or concurrently with, deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model. A large frontier developer shall transmit to the office a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk from internal use of its frontier models every three months or on another agreed schedule. A large frontier developer must have a current disclosure statement filed with the office, renewed every two years, and pay pro rata assessments to defray the costs of administering the article. A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident to the office within seventy-two hours; if imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, disclose to an appropriate authority within twenty-four hours. The act takes effect January 1, 2027.

mechanism.got: The attorney general may license an applicant as an independent verification organization if it shows independence from the AI industry and an adequate plan. The attorney general shall revoke an independent verification organization's license on specified grounds. A licensed independent verification organization shall implement the plan it submitted to the attorney general. A licensed independent verification organization shall revoke verification of a model or application whose developer or deployer fails specified requirements. The artificial intelligence safety advisory council is established in the office of the attorney general. An independent verification organization shall submit an annual report to the general assembly, the attorney general, and the auditor of state. Nothing in the chapter requires a model or application to seek verification from an independent verification organization. In civil actions for personal injury or property damage, a rebuttable presumption against liability applies only if all three listed conditions on verification, licensed risk and market segment are met.
